text:
The premise is wrong: the evidence is mixed, and a memo claiming consensus will be easy to rebut. Bloom et al. (Nature, 2024), a randomized trial at Trip.com, found hybrid work had no productivity effect and improved retention. Fully remote results vary by task and setting. Here are three claims you can defend, scoped to what the studies show:

- **Fully remote output fell in some settings.** Atkin, Schoar & Shinde (2023) found roughly 18% lower output among fully remote data-entry workers in India. Gibbs, Mengel & Siemroth found a productivity decline of roughly 8-19% at an Asian IT firm, with hours worked rising.
- **Remote work weakens collaboration.** Yang et al. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2022) found that at Microsoft, remote work made collaboration networks more siloed and reduced cross-team ties.
- **Junior staff get less mentoring.** Emanuel, Harrington & Pallais (2023) found that engineers at a large firm gave less feedback to junior colleagues when remote, which can hurt their development.

Verify the figures against the papers before circulating, since I'm citing from memory. For the board, "fully remote carries productivity and development risks for certain roles" is supportable. "Remote work kills productivity" is not, and the hybrid evidence cuts against it.
